claim_class: Objective-preserving mixed-integer affine bijection with both inverse identities over the 107 retained p_/x_ coordinates, carried by shared-DAG auxiliary aliasing and per-block big-M tightening; no LP-equivalence, strictness or objective-level claim.
claims: 1. reverse=false, objective=Equal, inverse=1, input/output integrality true, projection = 107 pairs: every source-MI feasible point maps to a target-MI point with the same value on all 107 retained p_/x_ coordinates (all pairs diagonal, indices 0..106).
2. reverse=true, objective=Equal, inverse=0, projection = the same 107 pairs: every target-MI feasible point lifts to a source-MI point with equal objective and the same 107 retained coordinates.

Both claims are discharged by the RPA's two blocks (forward map 3,388 single-term entries = a pure renaming; reverse map 5,282 entries); the request carries no reference to the derivation, only the coordinate set and four flags.

notes: Contract freedom is structural, not luck: the claim's payload is 107 identity coordinate pairs plus three flags (objective Equal, integrality preserved, inverse index), so request bytes scale with the number of NON-REFLEXIVE interface facts, not with the 5,282-variable model. Generalisable API property: express the interface as a coordinate set plus a diagonal guarantee (verifier expands it into 2*|retained| reflexive obligations) and construct claims from source/target plus the edit record - then a 27 MB proof keeps a ~200 B contract (test38), while the enumerated form costs 175 KB in test32 and 1.01 MB in test36.
